title: Gula Mineira
statementMd:
Today is an important day for Matheus "Mathias" Prates: he is taking his final exam in **AL2** (Cool Algorithms 2). He arrived early at the Federal University of Minas Gerais (UFMG) to study in the science library, but got so caught up in the review exercises that he is now late for lunch at his favorite campus restaurant, Gula Mineira.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/83d1cab9eb52a7edb775a66ce8b95e4395b76fdf.png)

Gula Mineira serves a self-service buffet with 𝑛n dishes arranged on a circular table. The table is represented by a circular list: position 𝑖i holds the dish identified by the positive integer 𝑝𝑖pi. Each dish appears at exactly one position.

Matheus has written down a sequence 𝑠s of the dishes he would like to take, in the order he wants to add them to his plate. Unfortunately, the restaurant is crowded, and everyone must move around the table in the same direction. If he is at position 𝑖i at time 𝑡t, he may move to the next position (𝑖+1i+1, or 11 if 𝑖=𝑛i=n), arriving at time 𝑡+1t+1, or leave the queue. Leaving and rejoining the queue takes 𝑘k seconds and allows him to rejoin at any position. Taking a serving of a dish, even repeatedly, takes no time.

Initially, Matheus is outside the queue and may join at any position for free. Every subsequent departure and reentry costs 𝑘k seconds.

He wants to take as many dishes from his wish list as possible, in the listed order, within 𝑤w seconds. More formally, he wants to take a longest possible subsequence of 𝑠s within this time limit. Dishes skipped in the subsequence need not be visited. Help him finish lunch in time for his exam!

## Input

The first line contains four integers 𝑛n, 𝑚m, 𝑤w, and 𝑘k (1≤𝑛≤2×1051≤n≤2×105, 1≤𝑚≤50001≤m≤5000, 0≤𝑤,𝑘≤50000≤w,k≤5000): the number of dishes on the table, the length of the desired sequence, the available time in seconds, and the time needed to leave and rejoin the queue.

The second line contains 𝑛n distinct integers 𝑝1,…,𝑝𝑛p1,…,pn (1≤𝑝𝑖≤𝑛1≤pi≤n), where 𝑝𝑖pi identifies the dish at position 𝑖i.

The third line contains 𝑚m integers 𝑠1,…,𝑠𝑚s1,…,sm (1≤𝑠𝑖≤𝑛1≤si≤n), the desired sequence of dishes.

## Output

Print a single integer: the maximum length of a subsequence of 𝑠s that Matheus can take within 𝑤w seconds.

## Note

**Explanation for example 2**

Here, 𝑛=5n=5, and dish numbers coincide with table positions (dish 𝑖i is at position 𝑖i), with 𝑘=2k=2 and 𝑤=5w=5. The diagram below shows the table, with arrows indicating the permitted direction of movement.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/05fd9929cc75ad93c6789853cddb29ab7516c921.png)

The desired sequence is 𝑠=(1,3,2,5,4)s=(1,3,2,5,4). Matheus can take 44 dishes within 𝑤=5w=5 seconds. It can be shown that no longer subsequence is possible.

**Explanation for example 3**

Since 𝑤=0w=0 and 𝑘=1000k=1000, Matheus cannot move along the queue or leave it. However, he may join directly at dish 22 and take it twice, using no time. This gives the subsequence (2,2)(2,2), formed by the first and third elements of 𝑠s: skipped elements need not be visited. Since no other dish appears more than twice, the answer is 22.
